items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: When the band started it's first engagement in the Zanzibar club... Billy Kyle(piano)

ctx.x: Came Christmas and the New Year of 1945, and John Kirby contacted me for a gig. There were a few changes from the original musicians

that had helped make Kirby the biggest little band in the world. In place of Russell Procope there was George Johnson, Bill Beason was the drummer and Ram Ramirez had replaced Billy Kyle. When we arrived at the place we were to play (which incidently was a concert) Buster Baily and I found a quiet place and he instructed me on how some of the numbers went. Of course, everything was written and no one that didn't have some experience in reading music could make it in that band and many others for that matter.

I made out alright and a few days later, Kirby asked me if I would like to go to California with him and that was another case of "had horn and would have travel". I had never been in California. I wasn't working and had no great love in New York to hold me there, so it was 'California, here I come' for me.
